title: Country Capability & Dependency Atlas
purpose: Turn country records from static profiles into relational state models: what a country has, can do, needs, depends on, supplies to others, is building and cannot do alone.

capability_record.rule: Capability means demonstrated or credibly available capacity within a stated time horizon, not aspiration alone.

dependency_record.rule: Dependency is directional and time-dependent. Mutual interdependence should be represented as two directed edges when both directions matter.

complementarity_record.purpose: Represent capabilities that only emerge through cooperation rather than pretending each country separately owns the full capacity.

resilience_tests: What fails first if the primary supplier/route is unavailable?
How quickly can an alternative be activated?
Does substitution require new physical infrastructure, legal approval, skills or capital?
Is nominal capacity actually available during a regional/system-wide shock?
Does a resilience intervention merely move dependency elsewhere?
Which capabilities are redundant, complementary or single-point-of-failure?

worked_system_cases.title: A debt ratio is a starting coordinate, not a fiscal diagnosis
worked_system_cases.lesson: France, Belgium and Denmark can be compared on the same Eurostat gross-debt definition, but the ratio alone does not tell the reader who holds the debt, when it matures, what public assets exist, what interest burden is, or how much administrative/productive capacity can absorb shocks.
worked_system_cases.reader_question: What additional relation would change the interpretation most: maturity, interest cost, tax base, asset position, holder composition or implementation capacity?

worked_system_cases.title: Energy dependency is a directed network, not one percentage
worked_system_cases.lesson: The 57% aggregate tells us net imports supplied a large share of EU gross energy needs under Eurostat's definition. It does not identify which fuels matter, which suppliers dominate, how much storage exists, what infrastructure constrains substitution, or how quickly dependence can be changed.
worked_system_cases.reader_question: If one supplier or route fails, what fails first and how long does substitution require?

worked_system_cases.title: Research spending becomes capability only through a conversion chain
worked_system_cases.lesson: Money is an input, not the capability itself. The useful world-system question is how funding is converted through institutions, people and infrastructure into research outputs and then into deployed technology, production or public capacity.
worked_system_cases.reader_question: Where does the conversion chain bottleneck: money, people, infrastructure, coordination, commercialization, procurement or deployment?

reader_rule: Every broad system noun should eventually open into actors → resources/flows → infrastructure → constraints → dependencies → capability → failure mode → evidence. A scalar becomes meaningful only after the relations behind it are visible.
